tour.title: This is the whole POC on one page
tour.text: {nodes} things from the code, the documents and three drawings, joined by {links} links. The four colours are the four parts of the project: the plant twin, data analysis, synthetic data, and the documents. Inside each part, things that belong together pull into islands; each island is one topic. Big dots have many links.

tour.title: The busiest hub: the 2D plant twin
tour.text: The twin is where everything meets. Its notes link the plant drawing, the eight plant stages, the stack heat model and the data files it plays back. If you change one rule in the twin, this is the neighbourhood that feels it.

tour.title: The eight plant stages hold the project together
tour.text: Heat-up with air, heat-up with forming gas, hot standby, fuel switch, part load, air-flow cooling, shutdown and trip purge. The analysis notebooks, the synthetic-day generator and the twin all lean on this one list.

tour.title: The plant drawing, read as a map
tour.text: Each dot here is a part of the real plant from the layout drawing: gas lines, heaters, reformer, burner, stack and inverters. The links follow the pipes, so the air path, the fuel path and the flue-gas path show up as chains.

tour.title: A link nobody wrote down
tour.text: The twin’s chain of linked stages and the synthetic-day generator’s “allowed stage changes” rule were written separately, but they describe the same thing. The extractor guessed this link (dashed line). Worth keeping the two in step.

tour.title: Every temperature trip ends in one place
tour.text: Exhaust, stack, afterburner and heater over-temperature limits all lead to the safety PLC’s emergency purge. Six of the nine real trips came from the exhaust limit.

tour.title: Which sensors can be rebuilt from the core 50?
tour.text: This island comes from the heatmap drawing. It links the 106 extra sensors to each stage and says whether they follow the 50 core sensors. Part load is the hard case: most sensors behave on their own there.

tour.title: What the outside world calls our stages
tour.text: Patents and papers (LG, Hanasaki, Toto, Bloom, IEC 62282) use other names for the same stages. Guessed links tie them to our hot standby, start-up and part load. Trip, hot idle and cold start were not found in the literature.

tour.title: Your turn
tour.text: Search for any tag or script, click a part or topic on the left, or press “How are two things linked?” to trace a chain between any two dots.
